correctness.rationale: PASS. Direct differentiation of \(F_{\delta}\) gives \(F_{\delta}''(u)>0\) on the whole domain and barrier blow-up at both endpoints, hence a unique minimizer. Evaluating \(F_{\delta}'(0)\) proves the exact threshold \(\delta_*=\tau\mu/(\mu x_2+\tau\zeta)\) when its denominator is positive and proves impossibility of zero-targeting when it is nonpositive. Substitution of \(\tau(\mu)=c\mu^a/(\mu^a+b)\) gives the three asymptotic regimes by elementary limits; on the critical line \(c\zeta=-b x_2\), exact algebra yields \(D(\mu)=x_2\mu^2/(\mu+b)\) and \(\delta_*=c/x_2\). The bundled checker independently evaluates representative strict regimes and verifies the critical identity with rational arithmetic.

The result shows that this exponent qualitatively determines whether the endgame's own local zero-target mechanism is asymptotically available, with a sharp transition and a nontrivial critical coefficient law. This directly informs a parameter choice that the source benchmarks empirically and is a structural interaction between two solver mechanisms rather than a routine recomputation or arbitrary numerical slice.
